# Framed Business Question

> **"What is the churn rate and average revenue per user (ARPU) across different customer segments, and how does ARPU differ between customers who churn and those who don't, for an Indian telecom operator?"**

---

# Section 1: Setup & Theme Configuration

```{python}
#| label: setup-eda
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from pathlib import Path
import warnings

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# Visual Styling
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", font_scale=1.05)
plt.rcParams.update({
    "figure.dpi": 130,
    "axes.titlesize": 13,
    "axes.labelsize": 11,
    "figure.figsize": (10, 5),
})

STATUS_COLORS = {"Retained": "#2b8cbe", "Churned": "#e41a1c"}
```

# Section 2: Load Processed Datasets

```{python}
#| label: load-processed
clean_path = Path("../data/processed/churn_clean.csv")
if not clean_path.exists():
    clean_path = Path("data/processed/churn_clean.csv")

df = pd.read_csv(clean_path)

trai_path = Path("../data/processed/trai_arpu_timeseries.csv")
if not trai_path.exists():
    trai_path = Path("data/processed/trai_arpu_timeseries.csv")

df_trai = pd.read_csv(trai_path)

print(f"Loaded Cleaned Dataset: {df.shape[0]:,} records, {df.shape[1]} features")
print(f"Loaded TRAI Benchmark Series:\n{df_trai.to_string()}")
```

---

# Section 3: Question 1 — Overall Churn Rate Analysis

```{python}
#| label: q1-churn-rate
total_subscribers = len(df)
churned_count = int(df["churn_probability"].sum())
retained_count = total_subscribers - churned_count
churn_rate_pct = (churned_count / total_subscribers) * 100
retained_rate_pct = (retained_count / total_subscribers) * 100

churn_summary = pd.DataFrame({
    "Status": ["Retained (Active)", "Churned"],
    "Subscriber_Count": [retained_count, churned_count],
    "Percentage (%)": [retained_rate_pct, churn_rate_pct]
})
print("Overall Base Churn Distribution:")
churn_summary
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-churn-donut
#| fig-cap: "Overall Subscriber Churn vs. Retention Distribution"
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5))
wedges, texts, autotexts = ax.pie(
    [retained_count, churned_count],
    labels=["Retained (89.8%)", "Churned (10.2%)"],
    autopct="%1.1f%%",
    startangle=140,
    colors=[STATUS_COLORS["Retained"], STATUS_COLORS["Churned"]],
    wedgeprops={"width": 0.45, "edgecolor": "white", "linewidth": 2}
)
plt.setp(autotexts, size=11, weight="bold", color="white")
ax.set_title("Overall Subscriber Base Churn Rate", fontsize=14, fontweight="bold", pad=15)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

# Section 4: Question 2 — ARPU Distribution Analysis

```{python}
#| label: q2-arpu-stats
def compute_arpu_stats(series, name):
    return {
        "Segment": name,
        "Mean (₹)": series.mean(),
        "Median (₹)": series.median(),
        "Std Dev (₹)": series.std(),
        "IQR (25%-75%) (₹)": f"{series.quantile(0.25):.2f} - {series.quantile(0.75):.2f}",
        "Min (₹)": series.min(),
        "Max (₹)": series.max()
    }

retained_df = df[df["churn_probability"] == 0]
churned_df = df[df["churn_probability"] == 1]

stats_table = pd.DataFrame([
    compute_arpu_stats(df["arpu_6"], "Overall Base (Month 6 - June)"),
    compute_arpu_stats(retained_df["arpu_6"], "Retained Subscribers (Month 6 - June)"),
    compute_arpu_stats(churned_df["arpu_6"], "Churned Subscribers (Month 6 - June)"),
    compute_arpu_stats(df["arpu_8"], "Overall Base (Month 8 - August)"),
    compute_arpu_stats(retained_df["arpu_8"], "Retained Subscribers (Month 8 - August)"),
    compute_arpu_stats(churned_df["arpu_8"], "Churned Subscribers (Month 8 - August)")
])

print("Comprehensive ARPU Distribution Statistics:")
stats_table
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-arpu-distribution
#| fig-cap: "ARPU Comparison: Boxplot and Density Distributions between Retained and Churned Subscribers"
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5.5))

# Boxplot (capped at 99th percentile for visual clarity)
p99 = df["arpu_6"].quantile(0.99)
sns.boxplot(
    data=df[df["arpu_6"] <= p99],
    x="churn_label",
    y="arpu_6",
    palette=STATUS_COLORS,
    ax=axes[0],
    width=0.45,
    boxprops=dict(alpha=0.85)
)
axes[0].set_title("Month 6 (June) ARPU by Churn Status", fontweight="bold")
axes[0].set_xlabel("Subscriber Status")
axes[0].set_ylabel("Monthly ARPU (₹)")

# Density Plot (KDE)
for status, color in STATUS_COLORS.items():
    subset = df[(df["churn_label"] == status) & (df["arpu_6"] >= 0) & (df["arpu_6"] <= p99)]
    sns.kdeplot(
        subset["arpu_6"],
        label=status,
        color=color,
        fill=True,
        alpha=0.35,
        linewidth=2,
        ax=axes[1]
    )
axes[1].set_title("ARPU Density Distribution (Month 6)", fontweight="bold")
axes[1].set_xlabel("Monthly ARPU (₹)")
axes[1].set_ylabel("Density")
axes[1].legend(frameon=True, title="Status")

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

# Section 5: Question 3 — ARPU & Usage Trend Leading Up to Churn

```{python}
#| label: q3-trend-table
monthly_arpu_trend = df.groupby("churn_label")[["arpu_6", "arpu_7", "arpu_8"]].mean().round(2)
monthly_arpu_trend.columns = ["June (M6)", "July (M7)", "August (M8)"]
monthly_arpu_trend["Absolute Change (M8 - M6) (₹)"] = monthly_arpu_trend["August (M8)"] - monthly_arpu_trend["June (M6)"]
monthly_arpu_trend["% Change (M8 vs M6)"] = (monthly_arpu_trend["Absolute Change (M8 - M6) (₹)"] / monthly_arpu_trend["June (M6)"] * 100).round(2)

print("Monthly ARPU Progression Across Good and Action Phases:")
monthly_arpu_trend
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-arpu-trend
#| fig-cap: "ARPU Decay Trajectory for Churners vs. Steady Revenue from Retained Subscribers"
months = ["Month 6 (June)\nGood Phase", "Month 7 (July)\nGood Phase", "Month 8 (August)\nAction Phase"]
churned_vals = [monthly_arpu_trend.loc["Churned", "June (M6)"], monthly_arpu_trend.loc["Churned", "July (M7)"], monthly_arpu_trend.loc["Churned", "August (M8)"]]
retained_vals = [monthly_arpu_trend.loc["Retained", "June (M6)"], monthly_arpu_trend.loc["Retained", "July (M7)"], monthly_arpu_trend.loc["Retained", "August (M8)"]]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5.5))
ax.plot(months, retained_vals, marker="o", linewidth=2.5, markersize=8, color=STATUS_COLORS["Retained"], label="Retained Subscribers")
ax.plot(months, churned_vals, marker="s", linewidth=2.5, markersize=8, color=STATUS_COLORS["Churned"], label="Churned Subscribers")

# Value annotations
for i, (r_val, c_val) in enumerate(zip(retained_vals, churned_vals)):
    ax.annotate(f"₹{r_val:.1f}", (i, r_val), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 10), ha="center", weight="bold", color=STATUS_COLORS["Retained"])
    ax.annotate(f"₹{c_val:.1f}", (i, c_val), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, -18), ha="center", weight="bold", color=STATUS_COLORS["Churned"])

ax.set_title("Monthly ARPU Trajectory Leading to Churn", fontsize=14, fontweight="bold", pad=15)
ax.set_ylabel("Mean ARPU (₹ / month)")
ax.set_ylim(50, 360)
ax.legend(frameon=True, loc="upper right")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

# Section 6: Question 4 — Segment-Level Breakdown

```{python}
#| label: q4-segment-table
segments = []
for dimension_name, col in [
    ("Customer Value Tier", "is_high_value"),
    ("Tenure Group", "tenure_group"),
    ("Recharge Frequency", "rech_freq_bucket_6"),
    ("Data Service Adoption", "data_user_label")
]:
    grouped = df.groupby(col, observed=True).agg(
        subscribers=("id", "count"),
        churners=("churn_probability", "sum"),
        churn_rate=("churn_probability", lambda x: x.mean() * 100),
        mean_arpu_good_phase=("avg_arpu_6_7", "mean"),
        mean_arpu_action_phase=("arpu_8", "mean")
    ).reset_index()
    
    # Clean segment names
    if col == "is_high_value":
        grouped[col] = grouped[col].map({1: "High-Value (Top 30%)", 0: "Regular (Bottom 70%)"})
        
    grouped.rename(columns={col: "Segment"}, inplace=True)
    grouped.insert(0, "Dimension", dimension_name)
    segments.append(grouped)

segment_summary_df = pd.concat(segments, ignore_index=True)
segment_summary_df["% Share of Base"] = (segment_summary_df["subscribers"] / total_subscribers * 100).round(2)
segment_summary_df["churn_rate"] = segment_summary_df["churn_rate"].round(2)
segment_summary_df["mean_arpu_good_phase"] = segment_summary_df["mean_arpu_good_phase"].round(2)
segment_summary_df["mean_arpu_action_phase"] = segment_summary_df["mean_arpu_action_phase"].round(2)

print("Segment-Level Churn Rate and ARPU Summary Table:")
segment_summary_df[["Dimension", "Segment", "subscribers", "% Share of Base", "churners", "churn_rate", "mean_arpu_good_phase", "mean_arpu_action_phase"]]
```

# Section 7: Question 5 — Macro Benchmark Comparison (TRAI 2014 vs Modern 2025)

```{python}
#| label: q5-macro-comparison
# Benchmark comparison table
trai_2014_row = df_trai[df_trai["report_year"] == 2014].iloc[0]

macro_comp_table = pd.DataFrame([
    {

        "2014 TRAI National Benchmark": f"₹{trai_2014_row['arpu_prepaid']:.2f}",

        "2025 TRAI National Benchmark": f"₹{trai_2025_row['arpu_blended']:.2f}"
    },
    {
        "Indicator / Metric": "Postpaid Monthly ARPU",
        "2014 TRAI National Benchmark": f"₹{trai_2014_row['arpu_postpaid']:.2f}",

    },

])

macro_comp_table
```

### Critical Note on Structural Break: Reliance Jio (September 2016)

> **IMPORTANT CAVEAT:**
> Direct numerical comparisons between the 2014 customer dataset and modern 2025 TRAI figures must be interpreted through the lens of the **Reliance Jio September 2016 structural break**:
> 1. **Tariff Architecture:** In 2014, consumers were billed on metered voice (per-minute) and expensive pay-per-MB 2G/3G data (e.g. ₹250/GB). In 2025, the market operates on bundled daily 4G/5G data quotas with unlimited nationwide voice.
> 2. **Voice Minutes Inflation:** Voice consumption escalated from 376 minutes/month (2014) to 1,026 minutes/month (2025) as calls became entirely free over VoLTE networks.
> 3. **Market Consolidation:** Over 10 active operators competed in 2014, whereas the market has consolidated into a private duopoly (Jio, Airtel) alongside Vodafone Idea and BSNL.

---

# Section 8: Summary of Findings

- **1. Baseline Churn Rate:** The overall subscriber churn rate is **10.19%** (7,132 churners out of 69,999 subscribers), reflecting a substantial baseline attrition rate.
- **2. High-Value Concentration:** The top 30% high-value subscribers (average recharge $\ge$ ₹477.50 in months 6 & 7) account for a lower churn rate of **8.28%** but represent **₹558.59 mean ARPU**, generating over 60% of total operator revenues.
- **3. Pre-Churn Revenue Collapse:** Churned subscribers exhibit a severe **62.95% drop in ARPU** from June (₹308.29) to August (₹114.23), while retained subscribers maintain steady growth (+6.16%, from ₹280.28 to ₹297.54).
- **4. Early Tenure Vulnerability:** Subscribers with tenure under 1 year suffer the highest churn rate at **15.85%**, compared to only **4.71%** among subscribers with 4+ years on the network (a >3x retention difference).
- **5. Data Plan Sticky Effect:** Subscribers actively using 2G/3G data plans exhibit lower churn (**8.72%**) and higher revenue (**₹368.52 ARPU**) compared to voice/SMS-only subscribers (**10.88% churn**, **₹239.16 ARPU**).
- **6. Macro Alignment & Jio Break:** The dataset's 2014 ARPU (₹283.13) represents active revenue-generating accounts that align realistically above the TRAI national blended average (₹115.72), which included hundreds of millions of low-spend secondary SIM cards. Modern TRAI ARPU (₹182.95 in 2025) reflects post-Jio market recovery following aggressive tariff restructuring.
